title: Which Way Is Down?
beats: Pun on down feathers; down is the direction things fall, but why do they fall
Turn the Sun into a black hole in Universe Sandbox to test what changes
Speeds time at 14 days per second, then real-time; compresses the Sun and the planets keep orbiting
Shrinking the Sun did not move the middle or the pull, so mass is the clue
Slaps a plastic ball and a steel ball to show mass as resistance to change in motion
Mass is intrinsic; it loves company, so gravity pulls centers together
Two baseballs one meter apart in empty space would collide after three days
Newton's formula in words: product of masses over distance squared times G; weight is this force
Scales display mass but sense force; mass versus weight confusion
Weight is mutual: the Earth weighs 180 pounds on me; pencil pulls Earth up a few trillionths of a proton
Astronauts are not weightless or in zero gravity; they fall around the Earth and lack apparent weight
Helium balloon weighed on a scale shows negative apparent weight; buoyancy from pressure
Air lifts you by an apple weight; Earth's bulge, spin, moon, lumpy mass each shift weight a little
Down is an uncombed mess; geoid as a bumpy level surface, exaggerated map
Down is a fluctuating vector, then asks why matter attracts matter
Hammer and feather drop fails in air (air-ror), then Apollo 15 vacuum clip
Newton's explanation: bigger mass gets more force and needs more; that is coincidence or not
Einstein: elevator accelerating up is indistinguishable from gravity; falling man feels no force
Retractable ID badge strings kept straight on a table versus a sphere: they converge without a force
Ribbon test: strip of paper lies flat only along straight paths; tries cone base ring, cone line, sphere latitude, equator
Geodesic named as a straight line on a curved surface
Curvature explains attraction only if things move; at rest, how does falling begin
One space dimension plus time on paper: space-time as a cone, the pencil follows a straight path and falls
Time runs slower lower down; electrons repulsion pushes you off the geodesic at the ground
Wheeler quote; Mercury's orbit as evidence
You mostly move through time, so down is toward slower time; Russell's cosmic laziness

metrics.misconception: yes: mass equals weight (5:26), astronauts weightless (7:39), heavy things fall faster (14:07)
metrics.brute_force: yes 4:13: two baseballs one meter apart for three days, and the Sun-as-black-hole simulation
metrics.examples: about 12, increasing from balls and pencils to planets and space-time
metrics.ending: Callback to the pun: down is toward slower time, then plugs

principles.1: confirmed: begins with the word down and feather drop; slapping balls, scale, balloon (0:00 to 8:36)
principles.2: confirmed: formula only in words (5:08); geodesic named at 19:33 after four tries; very few symbols
principles.3: not-observed: Universe Sandbox controls are shown but not taught
principles.4: confirmed: strings and ribbon on cone and sphere stand in for geometry of space-time (16:03 to 22:25)
principles.5: confirmed: ball slapping, scale and balloon, ID badges, paper ribbon
principles.6: confirmed: baseballs colliding after three days (4:36); every ribbon trial is dumb-but-physical
principles.7: confirmed: ribbon on cone base ring, cone line, curvy path, sphere equator, latitude (18:36 to 20:35) lets viewer deduce geodesics
principles.8: partly: speech stays fast; the later relativity beats are longer (16:03 to 22:43 is nearly 7 minutes of demos) and notation arrives late
principles.9: confirmed: ribbon test repeated across surfaces; weight mutual repeated for scale, pencil, ISS
principles.10: confirmed: tiny physical objects to Sun and planets to space-time with 1D+1 time
principles.11: confirmed: mass, then gravity, then weight, then apparent weight, then down varies, then why attract, then Einstein, then straight lines, then space-time
principles.12: confirmed: Apollo 15, Universe Sandbox, Wheeler, Russell, Mercury orbit
principles.13: confirmed: plain voice, steel ball and ribbon for a child, relativity and geoid for experts

new_moves.name: cheap-physical-instrument
new_moves.what: Builds a measuring device from household objects (ribbon straightness test, badge-string straight lines) that the viewer could rebuild

new_moves.name: remove-a-variable-first
new_moves.what: Changes one thing in a simulation (Sun to black hole) and shows what stays the same to isolate the relevant property

new_moves.name: dimension-reduction
new_moves.what: Collapses the problem to one space plus one time axis so it fits on a sheet of paper

new_moves.name: ridden-error
new_moves.what: Leaves the failed feather and hammer attempt in, calling it an air-ror, then fixes it with the vacuum clip

theory: The video builds a vocabulary by testing small physical things, each one removing a misconception, until a single idea (straight lines on curved surfaces) can carry the hardest step. The ribbon test is a thing the viewer can try, which makes geometry feel like an experiment.
velocity: Scene builder: ribbon-on-surface lab where the learner lays the strip on cone, sphere and plane and sees where it lifts
Orchestrator: prefer a remove-one-variable simulation as the first beat for causes
Ghost hands: hold the strip in hand and trace the geodesic
Learner model: tag each misconception (mass versus weight, weightless astronauts) and revisit with a new example
Evals: formula in words before symbols
quote: down is always in the direction of slower time.
